why: Must_not item 2 holds. Checks 1 to 3 all run the binary with fixtures, and only Check 4 reads a diff, which is fine because line 4 is not a behaviour line. Most PASS conditions follow their lines. For example, Check 1 compares against the old single-file output, matching "as for one file before". Check 3 breaks must_not item 1. Its PASS condition requires that "the missing-file run writes to stderr naming missing.jsonl". Expect line 3 only asks for an "error on stderr". Requiring the file name in the message is a stderr-content rule stricter than the line, close to the "exact stderr wording" example. A correct implementation whose message left out the path would fail this check.
